newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Parliament approves Portugal's EMU budget.
newsitem.headline: Parliament approves Portugal's EMU budget.

text.p: Parliament has approved the minority Socialist government's 1997 budget, which holds the key to its qualifying for the European Union's planned single currency.

Passage had been guaranteed by the pledges of two opposition parties to abstain in the vote on the package which cuts the state deficit in line with the target level for entry to Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
In a late-night session on Thursday, the 230-seat chamber gave the green light to the measures with only the Communist Party casting a negative vote.
The plan calls for the budget deficit to be cut to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), inside the three percent EMU ceiling, from around four percent in 1996.
Prime Minister Antonio Guterres has made qualifying for monetary union his government's top policy priority.

International confidence has grown that Portugal can make the grade, with local interest rates declining sharply as financial markets bet on its being included amongst the vanguard of EU countries to launch the single currency in 1999.
